net.lemnik.eodsql

Annotation Type Select


  • @Target(value=METHOD)
 @Retention(value=RUNTIME)
public @interface Select

    The @Select annotation is used to mark methods within a Query class that will return some form of data from database (typically a "SELECT" query. The Select annotation contains the SQL query that will be executed on the database

    Here is an example of how a @Select is used: 

         public class User {
         public Integer id;
         public String username;
     }

     public interface UserQuery extends BaseQuery {
         @Select("SELECT * FROM user WHERE id = ?1")
         public DataSet<User> getUserById(int id);
     }

    Any method annotated with @Select may return any one of the following datatypes:

    • the exact class to map - this will either return the first result found, or null if no results where returned.
    • the class wrapped in a DataSet which can be declared as either connected (default) or disconnected
    • the data object wrapped in a DataIterator, which may be declared to rubberstamp() (and thus only allocate one instance of the contained data object)
    • an array of the class to bind to
    • the class wrapped in a Set, List or Collection - these types have no connection to the database, the data is loaded into them and the result is returned.
    • a concrete implementation of a Collection class (must include a generic declaration of the contained type - Vector<User> is ok, but MyUserCollection is not
    • primitive types can also be mapped either as single objects, or as the contents of any of the above structures

    Columns that cannot be mapped to fields are ignored, as are fields that cannot be mapped to columns. @Select SQL uses the exact same query parser as the Update annotation, and so can also accept complex types as it's parameters, and insert their fields into the SQL query.

    Author:
    Jason Morris
    See Also:
    @Update, @Call

    • Element Detail

      • value

        public abstract String value
        The SQL query to execute on the database. The result set of the query will be mapped to the datatype specified in the method declaration. This attribute is used for convenience when none of the other attributes need to be explicidly set.
        Returns:
        the EoD SQL query to execute against the database
        See Also:
        sql()
        Default:
        ""

      • sql

        public abstract String sql

        The SQL query to execute on the database. The result set of the query will be mapped to the datatype specified in the method declaration. This attribute works in the exact same way as value(), but is used when you wish to specify values other than the SQL query.

        The SQL is partly parsed by the implementation, allowing for parameters of the annotated method to be used in the SQL statement. Selecting a specific User object from the database may look as follows:

        @Select("SELECT * FROM user WHERE id = ?1")
        User selectUserById(int id) throws SQLException;

        More complex introspection of the method parameters can be done using the bracketed syntax as follows:

        @Select("SELECT * FROM user WHERE email = ?{1.email}")
        DataIterator<User> selectUsersByUserEmail(User newUser) throws SQLException;
        Returns:
        the SQL query to execute against the database
        Default:
        ""

      • disconnected

        public abstract boolean disconnected
        Specify whether or not the DataSet resulting from a call to the annotated method will be connected to the database or not. This will generally only have an effect on DataSets.
        Returns:
        false by default
        See Also:
        DataSet, DataSet.disconnect()
        Default:
        false

      • rubberstamp

        public abstract boolean rubberstamp
        If rubberstamp is flagged as true, the annotated method must return a DataIterator, otherwise it will be rejected by the QueryTool. Rubber-stamping will cause the returned DataIterator to use a single instance of the data-object for all of the rows returned, instead of initializing a new one for each row. This can be used to save CPU time and memory, and is especially useful in display code.
        Returns:
        false by default
        See Also:
        DataIterator
        Default:
        false

      • readOnly

        public abstract boolean readOnly

        By deafult a DataSet returned by an @Select method is read only. If you set this to false the returned DataSet will implement the following additional methods:

        • List.add(Object)
        • List.addAll(java.util.Collection)
        • List.remove(int)
        • List.set(int, Object)

        It is considered a validation error for a method to have readOnly set false if it doesn't return a DataSet.

        Returns:
        true by default
        Since:
        1.1
        Default:
        true

      • cache

        public abstract Class<? extends DataSetCache> cache

        The cache class to be used by DataSets returned by the annotated method. This only has an effect of methods that return a DataSet type.

        The default DataSetCache implementation is ArrayDataSetCache, which uses an array to cache the row values. For larger ResultSets, you may want to look into a NullDataSetCache or using a DataIterator instead of the DataSet class.

        Returns:
        the DataSetCache type that the returned DataSet should proxy all of the returned objects through
        See Also:
        DataSet, ArrayDataSetCache
        Default:
        net.lemnik.eodsql.ArrayDataSetCache.class

      • fetchSize

        public abstract int fetchSize

        This is a hint to the database driver to suggest the number of rows to fetch in a single page of the ResultSet. This value directly corresponds to the Statement.setFetchSize(int) method.

        If this value is 0 (which it is by default) then the fetch-size of the underlying Statement will be left alone. This value (like the fetch-size of a Statement) is to be considered a hint to EoD SQL. The underlying MethodImplementation may choose to ignore this value.

        Returns:
        the suggested number of rows to be fetched at a time
        Since:
        2.1
        Default:
        0

      • into

        public abstract int into

        This attribute optionally allows you to populate one of the parameters of the annotated method instead of returning a new object. The value of this attribute must point to the index of the parameter to be populated. The first parameter is 1, the second is 2 and so on. The parameter must be a valid data-object, and thus may not be a Collection; array; primitive; etc.

        This attribute can be used to either refresh data that has previously been fetched from the database and/or to fetch new data into an object. This allows for a lazy-loading or fetch-group style of data loading from the database.

        Finally: a method selecting into an existing object may only return void or the same type as the specified parameter (in which case the parameter itself will be returned).

        Returns:
        0 by default to indicate that the method returns new objects instead of creating new ones
        Since:
        2.1
        Default:
        0

      • parameterBindings

        public abstract Class<? extends TypeMapper>[] parameterBindings

        The custom type bindings to be used on the parameters of this query. The binding is matched by position. The default type binding will be used for each parameter that has no parameterBindings entry or an entry that is of type TypeMapper itself.

        Since:
        2.2
        Default:
        {}

      • resultSetBinding

        public abstract Class<? extends DataObjectBinding> resultSetBinding

        A custom data object binding to be used on the result set of this query. The default value NoDataObjectBinding indicates that no custom binding is to be used.

        Since:
        2.2
        Default:
        net.lemnik.eodsql.spi.util.NoDataObjectBinding.class
